properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 4 at 10:19PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
UPDATED to raise the development potential of 94W to HIGH.

...HEAVY SHOWERS, GUSTY WINDS, AND CHOPPY SEAS LIKELY THIS WEEK FOR
KWAJALEIN AND NORTHERN MARSHALL ISLANDS...

A developing disturbance known as Invest 94W by the Joint Typhoon
Warning Center (JTWC) is located about 60 miles northwest of
Kwajalein. Development potential is rated high, meaning tropical
cyclone formation is likely within 24 hours. Scatterometry data
indicates 15 to 20 kt winds near Kwajalein, Ebadon, Ujae, Bikini, and
Rongelap, with winds up to 25 kt near heavier showers. Invest 94W will
be generally slow to move, remaining over the northern Marshall
Islands through Tuesday night. Scattered to numerous showers and
isolated thunderstorms may lead to locally heavy rainfall and
flooding. Through Friday, 4 to 6 inches of rain with locally higher
amounts are possible.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
difficult. Residents may need to reconsider plans for inter-island
boating as the week continues.

94W will continue to develop near Kwajalein over the next day or
two, so residents in the northern Republic of Marshall Islands (RMI)
should monitor the forecast for the next several days.

For more information on Invest 94W please see the Significant Tropical
Weather Advisory from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO
header ABPW10 PGTW. Also keep up to date with the latest information
from your local emergency management agency.

properties.instruction:

the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 4 at 4:50PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
A developing disturbance known as Invest 94W by the Joint Typhoon
Warning Center (JTWC) is located about 54 miles southwest of
Kwajalein. Development is rated medium, meaning tropical cyclone
development is likely beyond 24 hours. Scatterometry data indicates
15 to 20 kt winds near Kwajalein, Ebadon, Ujae, Bikini, and Rongelap,
with winds up to 25 kt near heavier showers. Invest 94W will be
generally slow to move, remaining over the northern Marshall Islands
through Tuesday night. Scattered to numerous showers and isolated
thunderstorms may lead to locally heavy rainfall and flooding.
Through Friday, 4 to 6 inches of rain with locally higher amounts is
possible.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
difficult. Residents may need to reconsider plans for inter-island
boating as the week continues.

94W will continue to develop near Kwajalein over the next day or
two, so residents in the northern Republic of Marshall Islands (RMI)
should monitor the forecast for the next several days.

For more information on Invest 94W please see the JTWC header
ABPW10. Also keep up to date with the latest information
from your local emergency management agency.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 3 at 8:35AM CDT until October 4 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Hastings NE
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by recent excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Along the West Fork Big Blue River in Southeastern York
County in east central Nebraska and Northwestern Fillmore County in
south central Nebraska...

* WHEN...Until 100 PM CDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 824 AM CDT, the gauge along the West Fork Big Blue River north
of Grafton was at 12.7 feet, which was above minor flood stage of
11.0 feet. As a result, fairly widespread flooding of pastures
and fields immediately adjacent to the river continues, including
downstream through the McCool Junction area. Based on trends at
the Grafton gauge, water levels appear to have crested and have
started a very slow, gradual drop that should continue over the
next few days. However, it now appears that the river will likely
remain above flood stage until at least sometime on Sunday,
prompting this Warning to be extended out farther in time.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
McCool Junction.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction: Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
